class.name: HDWII2CResource
class.brief_description: Virtual I2C slave on a (bus, address) - models one device on [code]/dev/i2c-<bus_index>[/code].
class.description:
Represents one I2C slave addressed by ([member bus_index], [member address]). The kernel decomposes every FSW transfer - including SMBus calls ([code]i2c_smbus_read_byte_data[/code], [code]write_word_data[/code], block ops, …) - into raw WRITE/READ messages before they reach the engine, so this resource only ever sees two asymmetric actions. That asymmetry is what keeps the kernel's shared stream framed: [constant I2C_WRITE] - master [i]to[/i] slave. A pure sink: the payload is appended to [member from_master] and [signal on_i2c_write] is emitted. This resource [b]never[/b] replies to a write - a response here desyncs the kernel's read loop. A zero-length write is an address probe / SMBus quick-command; note its presence, but still send no reply. [constant I2C_READ] - master [i]from[/i] slave. A request/response: the payload is a [code]u16[/code] little-endian byte count. This resource [b]always[/b] replies with [b]exactly[/b] that many bytes. The kernel hard-checks that the reply's [code]data_len[/code] equals the requested length and returns [code]-EIO[/code] to the FSW on any mismatch, so fill [member read_buffer] to the exact length (it is clamped/padded otherwise). The response carries no dev_id (the socket is strictly in-order, so the kernel knows which read it answers). The canonical "read register R" arrives as two frames in order - a WRITE carrying [code][R][/code] (latch your register pointer), immediately followed by a READ for the data. There is no repeated-start flag on the wire; just honor frame order per ([member bus_index], [member address]). [b]How to interface[/b] [olist] [*]Set the addressing properties: [member bus_index] and [member address]. Set [member device_name]. List buses contiguously from 0 so kernel-assigned adapter numbers line up with [member bus_index]. [*]Call [method HDWIResource.init] to register the device. [*]Connect [signal on_i2c_write] to consume bytes the FSW writes (latch a register pointer, store config, …). [*]Connect [signal on_i2c_read]; in the handler fill [member read_buffer] with [b]exactly[/b] the requested length [b]synchronously[/b] - the handler runs inline before the response is framed, so the stream desyncs if you defer it. [*]Connect [signal HDWIResource.on_send] to forward the READ response to the kernel socket. [/olist] [b]Example - a register-file slave (write sets pointer, read returns from it)[/b] [codeblock] var i2c = HDWII2CResource.new() i2c.device_name = "bme280" i2c.bus_index = 1 i2c.address = 0x76 i2c.init()
var registers := {} # register address -> byte value var ptr := 0 # current register pointer
i2c.on_i2c_write.connect(_on_write) i2c.on_i2c_read.connect(_on_read) i2c.on_send.connect(_write_to_kernel_socket)
func _on_write(address, data): if data.size() == 0: return # address probe / quick-command ptr = data[0] # first byte is the register pointer for i in range(1, data.size()): # remaining bytes are a register write registers[ptr + i - 1] = data[i]
func _on_read(address, length): var out := PackedByteArray() out.resize(length) for i in length: out[i] = registers.get(ptr + i, 0) i2c.read_buffer = out # MUST be exactly `length` bytes [/codeblock]

method.name: handle_i2c_write
method.description: Internal. Appends [param payload] to [member from_master] and emits [signal on_i2c_write]. Sends no response. Invoked by [method HDWIResource.dispatch_action] for [constant I2C_WRITE].

method.name: handle_i2c_read
method.description: Internal. Decodes the [code]u16[/code] LE requested length from [param payload], pre-zeroes [member read_buffer] to that length, emits [signal on_i2c_read] (synchronous, so GDScript can fill it), clamps/pads to the exact length, frames it, and emits [signal HDWIResource.on_send]. Invoked by [method HDWIResource.dispatch_action] for [constant I2C_READ].

method.name: get_group_type_representation
method.description: Builds the I2C section of the [code]CMD_SYNCH[/code] registration body: [code][type][num_bus][/code] followed by one entry per bus in ascending [member bus_index] order, each [code][bus_index][num_dev][/code] then each device's 32-byte name plus 1-byte address. Buses are emitted ordered so kernel-assigned adapter numbers line up with [member bus_index]. Called by the registry during sync.

method.name: lookup_i2c_device_id
method.description: Returns the 0-based registry slot of the slave at ([param bus_index], [param address]), or [code]-1[/code] if none is registered.

members.member: Adapter index this slave lives on - the [code]/dev/i2c-N[/code] the kernel assigns positionally during sync. Part of the routing key; list buses contiguously from 0 so the assigned number matches.
7-bit slave address (inner I2C header [code]address[/code]). Together with [member bus_index] it uniquely identifies the device.

Bytes the FSW has written to this slave ([constant I2C_WRITE]), accumulated in order. The simulation consumes these; clear by assigning an empty array. Each write also arrives live via [signal on_i2c_write].

The bytes returned for the current [constant I2C_READ]. Fill this inside the [signal on_i2c_read] handler. Length must equal the requested byte count (it is clamped/padded otherwise) or the kernel returns [code]-EIO[/code] to the FSW.

signal.name: on_i2c_write
signal.description: Emitted when the FSW writes [param data] to this slave. A zero-length [param data] is an address probe / SMBus quick-command. No response is sent for a write.

signal.name: on_i2c_read
signal.description: Emitted on each [constant I2C_READ], before [member read_buffer] is shipped, with the exact number of bytes the master wants. Fill [member read_buffer] with [param length] bytes synchronously before the handler returns - the response is framed and sent the instant this signal returns.
